prompt: Add the tag design-review to all the PDFs in the Product Specs folder whose descriptions mention the mobile redesign, are under 2 MB, and have exactly 3 comments on them, not counting replies.

references.name: the PDF to tag
references.description: every record the plural request selects (3)

claims.explanation: Same folder, description text and 3 comments, but it's a spreadsheet (.xlsx), not a PDF.
claims.alternative: a spreadsheet with the same description, size and comment count

claims.explanation: Tagged mobile-redesign, but its description talks about Q4 roadmap priorities, not the mobile redesign.
Same folder, description and comment count, but at 2.1 MB it is just over the 2 MB limit.
claims.alternative: the nearest size over the 2 MB line

mutation.note: the top-level-only comment count is replaced by a count over all comments regardless of reply status

claims.explanation: It has 3 comments in total, but one of them is a reply to another, so only 2 are top-level comments.
claims.alternative: the total comment count, replies included, instead of the top-level count
claims.contestable: reader: The file's comment_count field says 3, but the actual comment records show only 2 top-level comments (82141, 82142) plus 1 reply (82143, is_reply_comment=true) to 82141. Careful counting gives 2 top-level comments, not 3, so it fails 'exactly 3, not counting replies.' A reader who trusts the aggregate comment_count field without inspecting individual comments could mistakenly think it qualifies.

references.scope: All records in the supplied environment visible to the actor.
